newsitem.title: USA: Gore praises Detroit for empowerment zone.
newsitem.headline: Gore praises Detroit for empowerment zone.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore praised Detroit Monday for using its "empowerment zone" to spur economic development, saying the city's success is proof the federally sponsored program can be used to create good jobs and get people off welfare.

Gore, who came to Detroit for a two-day White House Community Empowerment Conference that starts Tuesday, said the federal government hopes to increase the number of empowerment zones around the country from the 15 that currently exist.
Gore singled out Detroit as having done the best job of using the project to bring new jobs to the city.
"No community in this country has made as big a success of empowerment zones as Detroit," Gore told reporters before a reception at Piston Packaging.

An auto parts supplier, the start-up company was co-founded in 1995 by Vinnie Johnson, a former Detroit Pistons basketball player, at a corner of General Motors Corp's now closed Cadillac plant in Detroit. About 80 percent of the firm's 178 employees live in the empowerment district.
Since the federal government designated the Detroit zone in 1994, local automakers and other manufacturers have announced plans to spend more than $2.5 billion in the area.
The most recent was Chrysler Corp, which announced plans last week to spend an additional $1.3 billion upgrading manufacturing facilities in the Detroit area, some of that in the empowerment zone.

Businesses that chose to locate in the city's 18.35-mile zone receive government assistance, including tax-exempt financing and an annual $3,000 credit for each employee who lives in the empowerment area.

Gore was joined in his remarks by Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer. The mayor criticized House Speaker Newt Gingrich and other Congressional Republicans for slashing federal funding in November 1994 that would have bolstered development in the empowerment areas.

Gore is scheduled to give the keynote address at the Third White House Community Empowerment Conference Tuesday morning. It is the first time the conference has been held outside of Washington D.C. He will tour various sites around Detroit, before delivering the closing remarks Wednesday and returning to Washington.
